title: Specie Insurance Policy Preamble, Cover, and Exclusions
summary: The page outlines the Preamble, Cover, and Exclusions of Tata AIG's Specie Insurance Policy. The Preamble establishes the insurance agreement based on the proposal form, premium payment, and compliance with terms, with liability capped at specified limits. The Cover section insures property against physical loss or damage at named locations or in transit within territorial limits, subject to exclusions and conditions, and only if other insurance does not cover the claim. The Exclusions section details non-covered events such as mysterious disappearance, inventory shortages, theft by principals or employees, insolvency-related losses, consequential loss, unattended vehicle loss, natural disasters, and gradual deterioration or manufacturing processes.

title: 2. EXCLUSIONS
summary: The text outlines the Specie Insurance policy wordings from Tata AIG General Insurance Company Limited. It begins with a preamble stating the insurance provision based on the proposal form, premium payment, and compliance with terms, with liability limited to the Policy Schedule. The cover section insures against physical loss or damage during the period of insurance at named locations or in transit within territorial limits, subject to exclusions and conditions, and only liable if other insurance fails. Exclusions list various non-covered events such as mysterious disappearance, theft by certain individuals, insolvency, consequential loss, unattended vehicle loss, natural disasters, war, government actions, nuclear risks, and pollution. Definitions are provided for 'Insured Property' (including money, valuables, and negotiable instruments) and 'Employee' (including various persons under control or compensation of the insured, directors, contractors, attorneys, and appointed individuals).

title: 3. DEFINITIONS

nodes.title: Insured Property
nodes.summary: The text outlines exclusions in a Specie Insurance policy, including loss or damage from environmental factors (aridity, humidity, light, temperature extremes unless caused by frost or fire), war and related hostilities, government confiscation or nationalisation, nuclear-related incidents (radiation, contamination, nuclear fuel/waste, hazardous properties, nuclear reaction), and seepage, pollution, or contamination. It also defines 'Insured Property' as various valuables like money, precious metals, gems, certificates, bonds, and negotiable items, and 'Employee' to include natural persons under contract or compensated, directors, contractor-provided persons, attorneys and their employees, and appointed persons acting on behalf of the Insured. Additionally, it provides company details for TATA AIG General Insurance Company Limited, including registration and contact information.

nodes.title: Employee

nodes.title: Specie Insurance Policy: Settlement Basis, Conditions, and Liability Limits
key_items: A. The basis of settlement will be:
1. Due diligence; 2. Transits; 3. Notice and proof of loss
nodes.summary: This page from TATA AIG's Specie Insurance policy wordings covers coverage for temporary employees, trustees, and non-compensated officers; the Aggregate Limit of Liability; the basis of settlement including agreed value for listed items, market value for unlisted items, and re-issue costs for securities with indemnity up to face value; the company's liability capped at applicable limits; timely coverage determination; and conditions requiring due diligence, compliant transits, and prompt notice and proof of loss within 90 days after policy expiration (and to police if crime suspected), along with duties to provide information, cooperate, and submit to examination under oath, with non-compliance due to intentional act or gross negligence limiting liability for undeterminable parts. It also includes insurer contact and registration details.

nodes.title: Specie Insurance Policy: Subrogation, Disclosure, Exposure, and Cancellation Terms
nodes.summary: This page from TATA AIG's Specie Insurance policy wordings covers four sections. Section 4 details subrogation, granting the company rights to recovery and requiring insured cooperation. Section 5 addresses incontestability and duty of disclosure, stating the policy is void for misrepresentation, non-disclosure, or fraud. Section 6 requires the insured to notify any increase in exposure, allowing the company to adjust premium or terminate with pro rata refund, and denies liability for unnotified increases. Section 7 covers cancellation: by the insured with written notice and short rate premium retention (with a table of rates based on duration), and by the company for misrepresentation, fraud, non-disclosure, or non-cooperation.
